usefulness.use_case: Explaining a wrong answer to the student
usefulness.example: add.c prints -2147483648 for the input 2147483647 1. The report shows the input, the expected 2147483648, what the program printed, and says to use long long.
usefulness.benefit: The student sees exactly which input breaks the program and how to fix it.

usefulness.example: add_copy.c is add_good.c with every name changed. The agent still finds a similarity of 1.00 and raises a flag.
usefulness.benefit: The teacher checks only the flagged pairs instead of every submission.

limitations.limitation: Short programs look copied even when they are not
limitations.example: add.c has a similarity of 1.00 with an answer from the qwen LLM, because the obvious 5-line solution is the same for everyone.
limitations.mitigation: A flag never lowers the grade; the teacher decides.

limitations.limitation: The readability score is the opinion of an LLM
limitations.example: add_syntax_error.c is neatly written but got 3/10 for one missing ';', while the more cramped add.c got 6/10.
limitations.mitigation: Readability is only 10% of the grade, and answers are cached so the score does not change between runs.
